forecast_results.prediction: AWS segment margin compresses 100-300bp in FY2026 vs FY2025 (35.4%) as D&A from the $131.8B capex wave flows through Technology & Infrastructure costs
forecast_results.evidence: Window is FY2026 full year (settles Feb 2027), so it is not yet elapsed — but both reported quarters run the OTHER way: Q1 2026 AWS margin 37.7%, Q2 2026 39.4% ($16.6B EBIT on $42.2B revenue), against the 35.4% FY2025 base. For the full year to compress even 100bp, H2 would have to average roughly 30% — an extreme reversal of the observed trend. Recorded as open on the letter of the window; the evidence to date runs strongly against it. [Amazon Q2 2026 results, IR release, 2026-07-30; CNBC AWS Q2 2026, 2026-07-30]

forecast_results.prediction: Q2 2026 consolidated EBIT lands in the $23-25B range (above the $23.4B consensus mid-point) driven by AWS acceleration and advertising strength
forecast_results.evidence: Actual Q2 2026 consolidated operating income was $27.5B, +43% YoY — ABOVE the stated $23-25B range, so the forecast as written did not hold. Its directional claim (above the $23.4B consensus mid-point) was correct; only its magnitude was too conservative, by ~10% at the top of the range. Falsified on the letter, directionally right. [Amazon Q2 2026 results, IR release, 2026-07-30]

lessons: The thesis's own falsification condition fired against it. The record stated: 'if AWS margin holds or expands, the hypothesis is wrong and the bull case at $247+ is live.' AWS margin expanded from a 35.4% FY2025 base to 39.4% in Q2 2026. On the engine's own stated terms the D&A billing-lag hypothesis is refuted, and the thesis is recorded broken.

Price outcome: entry $238.34 (2026-07-01, Capital IQ, pool-verified) to $270.87 (2026-07-31 close) = +13.65%, against an S&P 500 move of about -0.22% over the same window = +13.87pp benchmark-relative. As a Watchlist there was no executed position, so this is opportunity cost, not realised loss — but the call was 'do not buy at $238' with an expected return of -16.1%, and it was wrong in both direction and magnitude.

Review price $270.87 and index levels are web-sourced and indicative/unverified: AMZN close 2026-07-31 via stockanalysis.com price history (accessed 2026-08-01); S&P 500 7,483.23 on 2026-07-01 via CNBC market report and approximately 7,467 on 2026-07-31 via Trading Economics.

PROCESS ERROR, judged only on information available on or before 2026-07-10 (no hindsight): the disconfirming evidence was already in the engine's own files. earnings/03_margin-drivers.md recorded AWS margin RECOVERING 35.4% to 37.7% in Q1 2026, labelled Tailwind / High confidence, 'the new capacity is beginning to be monetized'; 99_earnings-synthesis returned 'Earnings accelerating' with a 'Balanced' setup. The master synthesis nonetheless headlined margin COMPRESSION at 60% probability. This is not a data gap and not bad luck — it is the synthesis inverting the sign of its own strongest module.

PROCESS ERROR, same information partition: the valuation base point put 40% weight — its single largest — on a sum-of-the-parts built on FY2025 TRAILING segment EBIT, while its own text conceded the trailing anchor 'understates the current run rate' and that 'the method I trust most is the SOTP-forward approach'. Peers ($258) and DCF ($207) alone blend to about $237, essentially the market price; the stale leg alone produced the $210 base and the negative margin of safety that drove the Watchlist.

PROCESS ERROR: the reverse-DCF judged the market's implied ~16.4% profit CAGR 'aggressive vs the 11.1% historical revenue CAGR' — testing forward SEGMENT-DRIVEN PROFIT growth against a decade of CONSOLIDATED REVENUE growth in a business where the segment driving profit was 18% of revenue and 57% of EBIT. Wrong metric, wrong level, wrong period. Realised consolidated EBIT growth in the next reported quarter was +43%.

PROCESS ERROR: capex was scored only as a future cost (D&A). The same run recorded, as its own 'strongest bull point', a $364B AWS backlog (+49% in one quarter) and management stating supply — not demand — was the binding constraint. Where capacity is sold before it is built, capex is closer to a booking than an expense; the market read the raised $220B guide as a demand signal and the shares rose.

The scenario set never spanned the outcome. Bull $247 (25%) / base $210 (45%) / bear $146 (30%) — a best case only +3.6% above the price, requiring FOUR conditions simultaneously (AWS >=35% growth AND D&A absorbed on a 6-month lag AND advertising rebounding to 32% AND North America units to 20%), against a bear needing one. ONE of the four (AWS growth, which printed 37%) moved the stock 15% in two days, past the top of the entire distribution.

What the process got RIGHT, and should not be over-corrected: the run wrote a genuine, dated, machine-checkable kill test and that test resolved cleanly; it never claimed the business was poor ('the franchise is worth owning, but not at today's price'); its Q2 EBIT forecast was directionally correct and ABOVE consensus; and the edge gate did its job — edge_score 35 < 50 capped confidence at 57, so the engine correctly reported that it had no proven edge. The defect is that a -16.1% expected return shipped as the headline anyway.

Single most important takeaway: the doctrine needed to prevent this was already written and simply unenforced. The multiples-first weighting policy (MODULE_RULES Scenario Construction §1) and the prohibition on a trailing SOTP carrying weight (06_sum-of-the-parts; Calculation Standard 10) were both hard rules, and the run broke both without anything noticing.

module_calibration_notes.most_responsible_for_decision: valuation — the -16.1% expected return is arithmetic on its $210 base fair value against a $238.34 price. No other module's score would have produced a Watchlist on its own.
module_calibration_notes.most_accurate_so_far: earnings — verdict 'Earnings accelerating', next-quarter setup 'Balanced', and a Q2 EBIT forecast ABOVE the consensus mid-point. Directionally right on every count; its only error was being too conservative on magnitude ($23-25B vs an actual $27.5B).
module_calibration_notes.missed_the_key_variable: valuation (weighted a trailing-earnings anchor at 40% while conceding in its own text that it understated the run rate) and the master synthesis (inverted margin-drivers' Tailwind/High reading of the very variable the thesis turned on).
module_calibration_notes.which_module_mattered_most_to_the_outcom: valuation and earnings. The realised outcome was an earnings event — AWS revenue acceleration and margin expansion — read correctly by the earnings module and then overridden by the valuation base point and the master synthesis. Governance and balance-sheet-survival were not material to this outcome.
module_calibration_notes.confidence_score_judgment: 57 was defensible and arguably should have been LOWER, not higher. Given only what was knowable on 2026-07-10, the run held an edge_score of 35 (below its own 50 gate), a valuation module confidence of 55 flagged for method dispersion of 52-148%, and a module (earnings) pointing the opposite way on the thesis's central variable. The gate correctly capped conviction; the failure is that a headline expected return of -16.1% was published on that basis at all. A 'no proven edge' read should suppress the headline number, not merely cap the confidence beside it.
module_calibration_notes.data_sufficiency_score_judgment: 82 was about right and is not implicated. Every fact needed to reach the correct read — the Q1 2026 AWS margin recovery, the $364B backlog, the supply-constrained management commentary, the forward consensus — was already in the pool on 2026-07-10. This was not a data-availability failure; it was a weighting and adjudication failure.
module_calibration_notes.evidence_partition_note: All process judgments above use only information dated on or before 2026-07-10 (the Q1 2026 10-Q, the Q1 2026 earnings call, the FY2025 10-K, the Capital IQ estimates workbook current to 2026-06-26). The Q2 2026 results dated 2026-07-30 are used ONLY for outcome fields (thesis_status, forecast_results, catalyst_results, risk_results, returns), never to downgrade the original reasoning.

memo_delta.summary: Amazon reported Q2 2026 on 30 July, one day before the memo's own named decisive test. Every number ran against the memo's central idea: AWS revenue grew 37% (fastest in 18 quarters), AWS operating margin EXPANDED to 39.4% against the 35.4% base the memo said would compress, consolidated operating income was $27.5B (+43%) versus the memo's $23-25B call, and capex guidance was RAISED to about $220B. The shares closed 31 July at $270.87 — above the memo's own bull case of $247. The memo's stated falsification condition has fired, so the thesis is recorded broken rather than merely at risk.

memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Amazon reported Q2 2026 on 30 July and it went against our call in every line that mattered. We argued that depreciation from the AI capex wave would squeeze AWS margins; instead AWS revenue grew 37 percent, its fastest in eighteen quarters, and the AWS operating margin expanded to 39.4 percent against the 35.4 percent base we said would compress. Group operating income was 27.5 billion dollars, above the 23 to 25 billion we forecast, and capex guidance was raised to about 220 billion with management saying capacity still cannot meet demand. The shares closed 31 July at 270.87 dollars, above even our bull case of 247. We wrote our own falsification test into the note - if the AWS margin holds or expands, the idea is wrong - and that test has fired. The thesis is recorded broken. We took no position, so this is opportunity cost rather than loss: plus 13.7 percent against the S and P 500 since our 238.34 dollar reference price. We are not re-rating the stock on this note. The valuation and earnings work needs redoing on the new numbers before we hold any view at all.
